thesis: Mike Zapata argues that value investing replicates the risk mitigation and assessment principles he learned during his decade as a Navy SEAL, where operations were viewed as low risk despite public perception of danger. He discovered this approach at Columbia University after reading Benjamin Graham's 'The Intelligent Investor,' which taught him that stocks are less risky when prices are significantly lower due to market emotion rather than fundamental value.
